Call To Us Panel: — Displays a phone icon and heading "Call To Us".

Call To Us Panel: — A horizontal divider separates this panel from the "Write To Us" panel below it.
Write To Us Panel: — Displays an envelope icon and heading "Write To US".
Write To Us Panel: — Displays static text "Fill out our form and we will contact you within 24 hours.".
Write To Us Panel: — Displays two support email addresses (customer@exclusive.com, support@exclusive.com) as clickable mailto: links.
Contact Form: — Your Name Field: Required text input, marked with a red asterisk (*).
Contact Form: — Your Email Field: Required text input, marked with a red asterisk (*); validates proper email format on submit.
Contact Form: — Your Phone Field: Required text input, marked with a red asterisk (*); validates numeric/phone format on submit.
Contact Form: — Your Message Field: Optional multi-line textarea (no asterisk), spans the full width below the three top fields.
Contact Form: — Send Message Button: Submits the form. — On successful submission: clears the form fields and displays a success confirmation (e.g., toast "Your message has been sent").
Contact Form: — Send Message Button: Submits the form. — On validation failure (missing/invalid required field): displays inline error messages under the respective field(s) and does not submit.
Contact Form: — Send Message Button: Submits the form. — On server/network error: displays an error message (e.g., "Something went wrong, please try again") and retains entered field values.
Footer: — Standard global footer (Subscribe, Support, Account, Quick Link, Download App, Copyright bar) is rendered as on all other pages.
Other information — Path to access the Contact page: Header navigation > Contact.
Other information — Submitted messages are stored/forwarded to the support team (e.g., via email notification or backend ticketing system) for follow-up within the stated 24-hour window.
Other information — Page must be responsive: the "Call To Us"/"Write To Us" panel and the form stack vertically on smaller screen widths.
Other information — No authentication state affects this page; it is identical for guest and logged-in users.

Navigate to the relevant screen
Check whether the reported discrepancy is present in the live UI

Click on the 'Your Name' input field and confirm placeholder text 'Your Name *' is visible
Type exactly one character (e.g., 'A') into the 'Your Name' field and verify the placeholder text disappears
Delete the single character from the 'Your Name' field and verify the placeholder text 'Your Name *' reappears

Repeat the same enter-one-character and delete steps for the 'Your Email' field (e.g., type 'B') and the 'Your Phone' field (e.g., type '1'), verifying placeholder text disappears on input and reappears on deletion
cypress_results.expected_result: Entering a single character into any of the three fields immediately hides the corresponding placeholder text, and deleting that single character immediately restores the placeholder text ('Your Name *', 'Your Email *', 'Your Phone *') in the respective field

cypress_results.scenario: Verify placeholder text is displayed in the Your Message textarea when the field is empty
steps: Open a supported web browser and navigate to the Exclusive platform URL
Locate and click on the Contact Us page link in the navigation or footer
Observe the 'Your Message' textarea field without clicking or interacting with it
cypress_results.expected_result: The Your Message textarea displays the descriptive placeholder text 'Your Message' when the field is empty and has not been interacted with

cypress_results.scenario: Verify placeholder text disappears and is not restored when the textarea contains user-entered text
steps: Open a supported web browser and navigate to the Exclusive platform URL
Locate and navigate to the Contact Us page
Click on the 'Your Message' textarea field and type any text (e.g., 'Hello, I need help')
Observe whether the placeholder text 'Your Message' is still visible alongside the entered text
cypress_results.expected_result: The placeholder text 'Your Message' is no longer visible once the user begins typing; the placeholder must not overlap or coexist with user-entered content

cypress_results.scenario: Verify placeholder text reappears after all entered text is cleared from the Your Message textarea
steps: Open a supported web browser and navigate to the Exclusive platform URL
Locate and navigate to the Contact Us page
Click on the 'Your Message' textarea and type any text (e.g., 'Test message')
Select all entered text using Ctrl+A (or Cmd+A on Mac) and delete it so the textarea is completely empty
Click outside the textarea to remove focus, then observe the textarea
cypress_results.expected_result: Once all text is removed and the textarea is empty, the placeholder text 'Your Message' reappears exactly as originally displayed, confirming the boundary between empty and non-empty states is handled correctly

cypress_results.scenario: Three contact fields display side-by-side in a three-column row above a full-width textarea on a standard desktop viewport
steps: Open a Chromium-based browser and navigate to the Exclusive platform Contact Us page
Ensure the browser window is set to a standard desktop width (e.g., 1280px wide)
Inspect the layout of the contact form visually and via browser DevTools
Verify that the 'Your Name', 'Your Email', and 'Your Phone' fields are rendered in a single horizontal row with each field occupying approximately one-third of the form width
Verify that the 'Your Message' textarea appears directly below that row and spans the full width of the form
cypress_results.expected_result: The 'Your Name', 'Your Email', and 'Your Phone' fields are displayed side-by-side in a three-column layout on the same row, and the 'Your Message' textarea is rendered below them at full form width, with no wrapping or stacking of the three fields observed

cypress_results.scenario: Contact form fields are missing or not rendered on the Contact Us page
steps: Navigate to the Exclusive platform Contact Us page on a desktop browser at 1280px viewport width
Simulate a scenario where one or more form elements fail to load (e.g., disable CSS to break layout, or use DevTools to delete a field element from the DOM)
Observe the resulting form layout
Check whether the remaining fields still attempt to maintain a three-column row or collapse incorrectly
Verify whether the 'Your Message' textarea is still present and full-width or also affected
cypress_results.expected_result: When a required field element is absent or the layout is broken, the form should either display a graceful fallback or the missing field should be clearly identifiable; the three-column row requirement is not met and this constitutes a layout defect that should be flagged

cypress_results.scenario: Three-column row layout behavior at the minimum desktop breakpoint boundary width
steps: Navigate to the Exclusive platform Contact Us page
Using browser DevTools responsive mode, set the viewport width to the exact minimum desktop breakpoint defined in the design spec (e.g., 1024px or the documented breakpoint value)
Verify that at this exact width the 'Your Name', 'Your Email', and 'Your Phone' fields are still displayed side-by-side in a three-column row
Reduce the viewport width by 1px below the breakpoint (e.g., 1023px) and observe whether the layout switches away from the three-column arrangement
Confirm that the 'Your Message' textarea remains full-width at the boundary width and just below it
cypress_results.expected_result: At the exact minimum desktop breakpoint width, all three fields must still appear side-by-side in a three-column row with the textarea full-width beneath them. One pixel below the breakpoint, the layout is permitted to change (e.g., stack fields vertically), confirming the boundary is correctly implemented

Locate and click on the 'Contact Us' or equivalent page link in the navigation or footer
Scroll to the inquiry/contact form section on the page
Visually inspect the submit button at the bottom of the form
Verify the button label reads exactly 'Send Message'
Verify the button has a filled background colour (e.g., solid red, black, or the platform's primary brand colour) that distinguishes it from surrounding form elements
cypress_results.expected_result: The button is rendered with the exact label 'Send Message' and is styled as a primary action button with a filled background colour, making it visually distinct from the rest of the form content

cypress_results.scenario: Send Message button is absent or missing from the contact form
steps: Open a supported web browser and navigate to the Exclusive platform URL
Navigate to the 'Contact Us' page
Inspect the DOM using browser developer tools and search for a button element with the text 'Send Message'
Simulate a scenario where the button element has been removed or its text has been altered (e.g., verify behaviour when the element is not present in the DOM)
Attempt to submit the form without the 'Send Message' button being available
cypress_results.expected_result: If the 'Send Message' button is absent or its label is incorrect (e.g., blank, 'Submit', or missing entirely), the form cannot be submitted via the primary CTA, and the missing or mislabelled button should be flagged as a defect — the page must always render the button with the exact label 'Send Message'

cypress_results.scenario: Send Message button label character boundary — label contains exactly the required text with no extra or missing characters
steps: Open a supported web browser and navigate to the Exclusive platform URL
Navigate to the 'Contact Us' page and locate the contact form
Using browser developer tools, inspect the inner text of the submit button element
Copy the exact text content of the button and verify its character count equals 12 characters ('Send Message')
Check for leading spaces, trailing spaces, line breaks, or hidden characters that could alter the visible or programmatic label
Verify the label is neither truncated (e.g., 'Send Messag') nor extended (e.g., 'Send Message ')
cypress_results.expected_result: The button label contains exactly 'Send Message' — 12 characters with no leading/trailing whitespace, hidden characters, truncation, or extra text — and the full label is visible without overflow or clipping within the button boundaries

cypress_results.scenario: Send Message button is displayed below the Your Message textarea and aligned to the right or bottom edge of the form
steps: Open a supported web browser and navigate to the Exclusive platform contact page
Locate the inquiry form containing the 'Your Message' textarea
Inspect the position of the 'Send Message' button relative to the 'Your Message' textarea
Verify the vertical position of the 'Send Message' button is below the bottom edge of the 'Your Message' textarea
Verify the horizontal alignment of the 'Send Message' button is flush with the right or bottom edge of the form container
cypress_results.expected_result: The 'Send Message' button is rendered directly below the 'Your Message' textarea and is aligned to the right or bottom edge of the form, with no other form elements positioned between the textarea and the button

cypress_results.scenario: Send Message button is absent or mispositioned when the contact form fails to render correctly
steps: Open a supported web browser and navigate to the Exclusive platform contact page
Simulate a partial page load or disable CSS stylesheets to observe unstyled or broken form rendering
Inspect the DOM and visual layout to check whether the 'Send Message' button exists in the page
If the button exists, verify whether it appears above the 'Your Message' textarea or outside the form boundaries
Attempt to interact with the button if it is mispositioned and record the behavior
cypress_results.expected_result: If the button is missing or mispositioned (e.g., rendered above the textarea or outside the form), the layout is considered a failure; the button must always appear below the textarea and aligned to the right or bottom edge of the form regardless of rendering conditions

cypress_results.scenario: Send Message button positioning remains correct when the Your Message textarea is resized to its minimum and maximum dimensions
steps: Open a supported web browser and navigate to the Exclusive platform contact page
Locate the 'Your Message' textarea and resize it to its smallest allowable height using the resize handle or browser developer tools
Verify that the 'Send Message' button remains positioned below the textarea and aligned to the right or bottom edge of the form at minimum textarea size
Resize the 'Your Message' textarea to its largest allowable height (or expand it to fill the maximum permitted area)
Verify that the 'Send Message' button dynamically repositions itself to remain below the expanded textarea and still aligned to the right or bottom edge of the form
cypress_results.expected_result: At both minimum and maximum textarea sizes, the 'Send Message' button consistently appears below the 'Your Message' textarea and remains aligned to the right or bottom edge of the form without overlapping the textarea or drifting outside the form boundaries

cypress_results.scenario: Visual separator is present and visible between contact info panel and contact form on standard desktop viewport
steps: Open a supported desktop browser (e.g., Chrome, Firefox)
Set the browser viewport width to 1280px (standard desktop resolution)
Navigate to the Contact Us page on the Exclusive platform
Inspect the area between the 'Call To Us' / 'Write To Us' panel and the contact form
Verify that a visual separator (vertical divider line, distinct spacing, or contrasting background) is rendered between the two sections
cypress_results.expected_result: A clearly visible visual separator (e.g., a vertical divider line, increased spacing, or a distinct background color/border) is displayed between the contact information panel and the contact form, making the two sections visually distinct from each other

cypress_results.scenario: No visual separator is present when the contact page CSS fails to load or separator element is missing from the DOM
steps: Open browser DevTools and navigate to the Contact Us page on the Exclusive platform at a 1280px desktop viewport
Using DevTools, locate the separator element (e.g., a div with a divider class or a CSS border/background applied between the two panels)
Remove the separator element from the DOM or disable its associated CSS rule (e.g., set 'display: none' or delete the border/background property)
Observe the layout between the 'Call To Us' / 'Write To Us' panel and the contact form
cypress_results.expected_result: Without the separator element or its styling, the two sections appear merged or indistinguishable, confirming that the separator is a required visual component; the page should not pass QA validation in this state and the missing separator should be flagged as a defect

cypress_results.scenario: Visual separator behavior at the boundary viewport width where desktop layout transitions to a narrower (tablet/mobile) layout
steps: Open a supported browser and navigate to the Contact Us page on the Exclusive platform
Open DevTools and set the viewport width to the exact breakpoint where the desktop layout ends (e.g., 1024px or the defined desktop breakpoint minus 1px, such as 1023px)
Inspect whether the vertical visual separator between the contact info panel and the contact form is still visible at this exact boundary width
Reduce the viewport by 1px below the breakpoint (e.g., 1023px if breakpoint is 1024px) and verify the separator behavior changes appropriately for narrower viewports
Increase the viewport by 1px above the breakpoint (e.g., 1025px) and confirm the separator is fully visible in desktop layout
cypress_results.expected_result: At the exact desktop breakpoint width, the visual separator is visible and the desktop two-column layout is intact. One pixel below the breakpoint, the layout collapses to a stacked (mobile/tablet) view where the vertical separator is no longer required to be present. One pixel above the breakpoint, the separator is clearly rendered, confirming the responsive boundary behaves as designed
